messages:
Maya: Heads-up — I ran a quick apples-to-apples against the new kernel picker and saw a consistent oddity around KV cache hits vs misses. Sharing logs and a tiny repro.
Nick: Can you summarise the observable delta? p95/p99 or TTFT changes?
Maya: p95 TTFT increases ~12% when KV cache hit ratio drops below ~65%. QPS/goodput unaffected for long sequences, but short-turn chats show higher TTFT. p99 tails also broaden.
Sasha: Interesting — is the kernel selector switching to the slower matmul path when sequence length varies? We saw heuristics that prefer robust kernels at moderate lengths.
Maya: Exactly what I suspected. When the replay harness injects sequences with a bimodal length distribution the selector flips kernels mid-run. That interacts badly with KV cache prefetching heuristics.
Cheng: Can you paste the replay config? we should compare with the synthetic traffic used earlier.
Maya: Paste below — this is the tiny harness snippet I used:
```
--replay-mode=trace
--trace-file=short+long-seqs.jsonl
--arrival-dist=poisson
--batching=adaptive
--kernel-policy=auto
--kv-cache-policy=local-prefetch
```
Nick: That `local-prefetch` is probably the culprit — it assumes stable kernel across adjacent requests. Under replay where kernel flips, prefetch overhead causes extra serialization.
Sasha: So we need two experiments:
1) Synthetic steady-state (mono-length) with deterministic kernels to measure baseline TTFT/TPOT.
2) Replay (bimodal lengths) with the real-world arrival distribution to expose selector instability.
Maya: Agreed. Also propose instrumenting the kernel selector to emit events: kernel_choice, reason, and sequence_len at decision time. Minimal change and we can correlate with TTFT spikes.
Cheng: I can add logs. How about we standardize metrics collection names? Use TTFT_ms, TPOT_ms, p95_TTFT_ms, p99_TTFT_ms, goodput_tokens/s, qps_req/s.
Nick: +1. Also tag runs with `traffic_profile` (synthetic/replay), `kernel_policy`, and `kv_policy` so we can group in the dashboard.
DevBot: test-run #409 queued by @Maya using profile=replay-bimodal. ETA ~12m. :robot_face:
Maya: Running a short smoke now, will post p95/p99 samples. If this reproduces, next step is to make kernel-selector sticky for short-lived sessions or make kv-prefetch conservative.
Sasha: Another angle — measure cache warmup latency separately. Goodput can hide TTFT issues when throughput is saturated.
Maya: Initial smoke results (median of 3 runs): TTFT_p95: 72ms -> 81ms (+12%), TTFT_p99: 143ms -> 175ms (+22%). Goodput stable ~620 tokens/s.
Nick: That's pretty convincing. Can we avoid global kernel flip by adding hysteresis: require 2 consecutive windows before switching? That might reduce sensitivity.
Cheng: I'll prototype hysteresis and a `prefer-cache-friendly` kernel flag. If prefetching and kernel choice can be co-scheduled, should help.
Maya: Great. I'll open a short PR with selector instrumentation + a benchmark harness tweak so synthetic/replay configs are shared. Assigning follow-ups:
- Cheng: implement hysteresis + flag (owner)
- Maya: add instrumentation, re-run full replay suite (owner)
- Nick: update dashboards and add tags (owner)
Sasha: One more ask — include a tiny `metrics.md` snippet in the PR that defines TTFT vs TPOT vs goodput, so reviewers are aligned.
Maya: Will do. Quick defs I used:
TTFT_ms = time from request accepted by runtime to first emitted token.
TPOT_ms = time from request accepted to final token output (end-to-end latency).
goodput_tokens/s = successfully emitted user tokens / wall_time (excludes internal retries).
qps_req/s = requests accepted / wall_time.
p95/p99 computed over per-request TTFT_ms samples.
Nick: Perfect. Let's reconvene after the replay-suite run. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
